answer_raw:
Your US accounts will generally remain subject to US law, but your Brazilian apartment will be subject to Brazilian legal processes and rules.

**Brazilian assets** like an apartment fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of Brazilian authorities, regardless of your nationality or domicile [2]. To transfer the title of a Brazilian property to your heirs, they must undergo a formal Brazilian probate process known as an *inventário* [2]. Foreign wills or foreign court orders cannot be used to bypass this process to transfer real estate or release frozen Brazilian bank accounts [2]. 

**Brazilian inheritance rules**—specifically "forced heirship" (*legitima*)—will apply to the assets located within Brazil. Under Brazilian law, at least **50% of the estate** must be distributed to compulsory heirs (such as children) [1]. While your US-based accounts are handled under US jurisdiction, the Brazilian portion of your estate must comply with these local distribution requirements [1][2].

The impact on your US-based heirs depends on how the US and Brazil treat the transfer of assets. While the Brazilian *inventário* settles the local property, your heirs will still need to manage the US side of the estate according to US tax and probate laws. You should consult a cross-border estate attorney to coordinate how the Brazilian *legitima* interacts with your US-based will to avoid legal friction between the two jurisdictions.

question: If I move to Brazil on a retirement visa and die there, what happens to my US accounts and a Brazilian apartment I bought? Do my heirs in the US get hit with Brazilian inheritance rules?
